lines.name: BART Silicon Valley Phase II
lines.summary: VTA's six-mile extension of BART from Berryessa through downtown San José to Santa Clara, with three underground stations, one at-grade station and a rail yard, built around a single tunnel about 53 feet across. Its adopted budget is $12.7 billion. Early works are under way at the tunnel launch site, but the federal grant that would pay for about 40% of it is not yet signed, and service is scheduled for 2039 (VTA aims for 2037).

links.label: Project record in the megaprojects map

lines.notes: Status translated from BAM's stage (infrastructure): BAM stage 'infrastructure': early construction ahead of tunneling (launch structure dug, demolition and utility relocation at station sites). Stage note at 2026-10-07: Early construction, ahead of tunneling. Crews finished excavating the West Portal launch structure for the tunnel boring machine in early September 2026, and demolition and utility relocation are under way at station sites. In August 2026 VTA signed a restated tunnel contract and gave notice to proceed with pre-tunneling work only. The federal grant agreement that would fund most of the line is not yet signed (VTA's target is late 2027), the boring machine is in storage in Germany with delivery expected in the second half of 2027, and FTA's oversight consultant rates the project high risk while VTA re-baselines its cost and schedule.

lines.name: California High-Speed Rail: San Francisco to San Jose
lines.summary: The Bay Area end of California's high-speed rail line. Rather than building new tracks up the Peninsula, high-speed trains would share Caltrain's newly electrified corridor for about 49 miles from San Francisco to San Jose, stopping at Fourth and King (and later the Salesforce Transit Center via The Portal), Millbrae for SFO, and San Jose Diridon. The route was environmentally approved in 2022, but no construction has started and the Authority's current plan reaches the Bay Area by 2039.

links.label: Project record in the megaprojects map

lines.notes: Status translated from BAM's stage (entitled): BAM stage 'entitled': environmentally cleared (ROD Oct 2022); right-of-way, design and station work not started. Stage note at 2026-10-07: Environmentally cleared: the Authority's Board certified the Final EIR/EIS and approved the route in August 2022, and the Record of Decision followed in October 2022. No construction has started. The 2026 Business Plan's schedule lists right-of-way, design, and the Fourth and King, Millbrae and San Jose station work as 'not started'. It plans for trains to reach the Bay Area over upgraded shared tracks by 2039 in its San Francisco–Bakersfield scenario. That depends on funding and on agreements with Caltrain and partners, including for the San Jose to Gilroy line. Until The Portal is built, Fourth and King is the interim terminus.

lines.name: SMART Cloverdale extension
lines.summary: The last leg of the voter-approved SMART system: about 13.5 miles of out-of-service railroad from north of Healdsburg to Cloverdale, with new stations at Geyserville (adopted in August 2026) and Cloverdale. It was environmentally cleared with the rest of the line and is in the regional plan, but it has no construction funding yet.

links.label: Project record in the megaprojects map

lines.notes: Status translated from BAM's stage (proposed): BAM stage 'proposed': environmentally cleared but not yet fully funded, with no construction schedule. Stage note at 2026-10-08: Shown as proposed: environmentally cleared but not yet fully funded, with no construction schedule; SMART says the Cloverdale station will be completed when funding becomes available. SMART's 2006 EIR and 2008 SEIR covered the whole 70-mile corridor to Cloverdale. On Aug 19, 2026 the Board adopted a Geyserville station into SMART's program and approved it as a station project of its own, statutorily exempt from CEQA as a passenger rail project (Public Resources Code 21080.25, as amended by SB 71), to be advanced as part of the extension to Cloverdale; SMART filed the notice of exemption the next day. The extension is in Plan Bay Area 2050+, adopted in March 2026, with a $353 million capital cost and a 2025-2035 opening period, but SMART says it still needs state and federal grants and has applications pending or in development. SMART puts Healdsburg to Cloverdale at about 18 miles, and a Geyserville station at about the midpoint lets it split that into two smaller projects that may compete better for grants. The Cloverdale station site is listed as to be determined, and the Healdsburg design-build contract includes options to continue north if more grants are secured.

lines.name: SMART Healdsburg extension
lines.summary: The next step north for SMART's trains: about nine miles of railroad, idle for decades, rebuilt from today's end of the line at Windsor through Healdsburg, with a new Healdsburg station, a replacement Russian River rail bridge and the SMART Pathway alongside. It is funded at about $269 million, in design, and planned to open in late 2028; where the Healdsburg station goes is being reconsidered.

links.label: Project record in the megaprojects map

lines.notes: Status translated from BAM's stage (entitled): BAM stage 'entitled': funded, environmentally cleared and in design; construction hasn't started. Stage note at 2026-10-08: Funded, environmentally cleared and in design; construction hasn't started. The route is covered by SMART's 2006 EIR and 2008 SEIR for the 70-mile system; the Board adopted an addendum for this segment on Dec 17, 2025, and the California Transportation Commission, as a responsible agency, accepted it and approved the project for future consideration of funding on Jan 29, 2026. The progressive design-build team, under contract since September 2025, had prepared 50% design documents by September 2026, and utility potholing began in April 2026. The first construction package, Windsor Station to Front Street, is due for award in October 2026, with construction starting in spring 2027; a second package, Front Street to North Street, includes the station. SMART is also asking the public where the Healdsburg station should go: the historic Depot/Hudson Street site the City prefers (reaffirmed in September 2026), or a Downtown site on Vine Street about 0.45 mile away. Service is planned for December 2028.

lines.name: The Portal (Downtown Rail Extension)
lines.summary: A rail tunnel to bring Caltrain, and later high-speed rail, from the Fourth and King terminus about 1.3 miles into the Salesforce Transit Center, whose two-level underground train box was built for it and has stood empty since 2018. It adds an underground station at Fourth and Townsend. The $8.3 billion project is environmentally cleared and in federal engineering review, with a $3.38 billion federal grant in sight. It still needs the rest of its local and state funding, and TJPA forecasts service in late 2036.

links.label: Project record in the megaprojects map

lines.notes: Status translated from BAM's stage (entitled): BAM stage 'entitled': environmentally cleared, in FTA's Engineering phase, not under construction or fully funded. Stage note at 2026-10-07: Environmentally cleared and in the Engineering phase of FTA's Capital Investment Grants program since May 2024, but not yet under construction or fully funded. Design is at 30% for the tunnel and stations and 60% for the early works. Right-of-way appraisals are under way, and proposals for the civil and tunnel progressive design-build contract are due Oct 9, 2026. The Full Funding Grant Agreement is targeted for July 2027. TJPA says utility relocation construction will start in 2028 and forecasts that the line will be ready for service on Nov 17, 2036.

lines.name: Valley Link
lines.summary: A new passenger rail line along the I-580 corridor linking BART at Dublin/Pleasanton with ACE commuter trains at Vasco Road in Livermore, so riders from the San Joaquin Valley can change trains across a platform instead of driving over the Altamont Pass. The first 11 miles, with three stations and battery-electric trains, are environmentally cleared and in design; an extension to Mountain House is cleared but unfunded.

links.label: Project record in the megaprojects map

lines.notes: Status translated from BAM's stage (entitled): BAM stage 'entitled': environmentally cleared and in design; no construction yet. Stage note at 2026-10-07: Environmentally cleared and in design; no construction yet. The Authority certified the Subsequent EIR for the 22-mile Phase 1 in October 2024 and FTA issued a FONSI on May 27, 2025. In June 2025 the Board split delivery after cost increases at 30% design, starting with the 11-mile Phase 1A to Vasco Road; a joint CEQA addendum and NEPA re-evaluation for the 1.5-mile connection from I-580/First Street to Vasco Road is targeted for fall 2026. A CM/GC preconstruction contract went to Kiewit in June 2026. Construction funding is not yet secured: the Authority is preparing to ask FTA to enter the Capital Investment Grants Engineering phase.

lines.name: B Geary
lines.summary: A shuttle on Geary from 10th to 33rd Aves on Muni's first day, then from June 25, 1913 the Ferry Building to Ocean Beach, out Market and Geary and by 33rd Ave, Balboa St, 45th Ave and Cabrillo St.
lines.fate_note: Buses replaced the B after December 29, 1956, leaving only the J, K, L, M and N streetcar lines (Callwell p. 48).
lines.notes: Muni's own reports give June 24 or 25, 1913 for the run to the beach; Callwell gives June 25. From March 22, 1949 it turned at the Transbay Terminal by 1st and Fremont Sts (Callwell p. 46); that loop isn't drawn, nor the Ferry Building loop. Whether it kept the 33rd Ave, Balboa St and 45th Ave route to the end isn't sourced yet.

lines.name: Berkeley line

operators.name: Key System (the San Francisco, Oakland & San Jose Railway and its successors)

lines.summary: The Key Route's first line, from its pier to downtown Berkeley by Adeline Street and Shattuck Avenue; cut back to Alcatraz Avenue in 1933, then from 1941 over the Southern Pacific's old tracks to Northbrae and, from 1942, through the Northbrae Tunnel to The Alameda.
lines.notes: Letters were given to the lines in 1939. By 1933 the line ran to University Avenue, not Center Street; when it was extended isn't sourced, and that last stretch isn't drawn. The day of the 1933 cutback isn't sourced. The last trains ran in 1958 (HAER); April 19 or 20, 1958 is given only by later sources.

segments.name: Key Route Pier
segments.note: Over the Key Route pier to its ferries until January 15, 1939
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 3 m)); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The trestle runs straight from the shore, then curves to the ferry terminal.
segments.notes: Ferry trains ran to its end until the Bay Bridge opened to trains in January 1939; from then its land end carried the bridge trains. A 1933 fire is relayed via Wikipedia only.

segments.name: Transbay Terminal loop, San Francisco
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (23 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The loop as the 1950 sheet draws it ("KEY SYSTEM"): from the approach, north along the west side to the terminal's west end, through the six-track station facing Mission Street, around the east end and back south. Trains ran counter-clockwise, arriving at the station's east end.

segments.name: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge, lower deck
segments.method: Joined to bbr-sf-loop at its start; then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 2 m)); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (8 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From Rincon Hill across the bridge's lower deck, through the Yerba Buena Island tunnel, to where the tracks left the bridge on its south side at the Oakland end. The 1946-50 sheets draw the bridge, not the tracks on it; the tracks were on the south half of the lower deck.

segments.name: East Bay approach and yards
segments.method: Joined to bbr-bridge at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the south side of the bridge approach ("KEY SYSTEM" on the 1949 sheet) past the toll plaza to the East Bay yards, where the Key System's and the Interurban's tracks divided.

segments.name: East Bay yards to the old pier line
segments.method: Joined to bbr-east-approach at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then joined to key-pier at its start. From the East Bay yards over the bridge approach to the north side of the mole ("TRANSIT LINES" on the 1949 sheet), meeting the old pier line.

segments.name: Pier approach and subway to Poplar Junction
segments.method: Joined to key-pier at its start; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From the pier's land end under the Southern Pacific main line (the 1903 subway) to Poplar Junction, along the line the 1949 sheet draws there.

segments.name: Yerba Buena Avenue to San Pablo Avenue
segments.method: Joined to key-trunk-shore at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along Yerba Buena Avenue to the station at San Pablo Avenue.

segments.method: Joined to key-yerba-buena at its end; then along today's Linden Street centerline from -122.27900,37.83100 to -122.27530,37.83550 (509 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 250 m where the street is cut today); then given point by point; checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). lines.name: California Pacific trains, Vallejo to Calistoga
lines.summary: Trains from the ferry at South Vallejo by Napa Junction, Napa, Yountville and St. Helena to Calistoga; by 1929, one round trip a day.
lines.fate_note: Discontinued on or about June 1929, with the ferry from Vallejo Junction, in favour of the Southern Pacific's own motor coaches (CRC Decision No. 21194).
lines.notes: The Napa Valley Railroad ran from steamers at Soscol to Napa from July 11, 1865, and reached Calistoga in October 1868 (Napa County history); the California Pacific, which bought it in 1869, joined it at Napa Junction from Vallejo in 1868-69, at "sundry dates" its own return gives no details of. So when trains first ran from Vallejo to Calistoga isn't sourced: the map draws them from 1880, the first date a source shows the line (decision 20), in the lighter tint. Soscol and the line of 1865 into Napa by Main Street aren't drawn.

running.note: "Branches: Napa Junction to Calistoga 34.65" miles.
"Napa Junction to Calistoga 34.48" miles, in the California Pacific's mileage.
"Napa Junc. to Calistoga", in the Southern Pacific's mileage.

Today's track from the end of rail at South Vallejo, near the old wharf on the 1898 Karquines sheet, to Napa Junction.
segments.notes: The California Pacific's line north from its wharf at South Vallejo, built in 1868-69 (the railroad reported only "sundry dates"), still in place today.

segments.notes: The California Pacific's junction of its line to Sacramento with the Napa Valley line.

segments.name: Napa Junction to Yountville, by Napa
segments.method: Along today's track from -122.25064,38.18708 to -122.35769,38.39694 (26340 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1 rail); checked on USGS Cuttings Wharf 1:24,000 (1951), USGS Napa 1:24,000 (1951) and USGS Yountville 1:24,000 (1951). Today's track, which the 1951 sheets show the railroad on, to where it leaves the old line south of Yountville.
segments.notes: Up the valley by Napa. The Napa Valley Railroad's first line of 1865 ran from Soscol, on the river south of Napa, and entered the town by Main Street; the line was moved to East Napa on January 4, 1877 (Napa County history, pp. 76-80). Today's track is the later line.

lines.name: Central Pacific trains, Oakland to Sacramento by Niles and the Altamont Pass
lines.summary: The first railroad to the bay: the Western Pacific's line of 1869 from Oakland Point by Melrose, San Leandro, Hayward and Niles, through Niles Canyon and over the Altamont Pass to Stockton and Sacramento.
lines.fate_note: All regular passenger trains between Tracy and Elmhurst via Niles ended on or about January 1941 (CRC Decision No. 33781); the line from Oakland to Niles still carries trains.
lines.notes: Opens with the first through passenger train from Oakland Point (Halley); the railroad's own return gives "about December 1, 1869". From September 8 to November 8, 1869 its trains ran from San Leandro to the Alameda wharf over the San Francisco & Alameda, not drawn. Through Oakland it follows the electric lines' Seventh Street and Melrose segments, the second of them approximate, so a short gap is left before today's track.

segments.name: Oakland Mole
segments.note: The Oakland Mole, from February 1881 (Wood, 1883, p. 631); before it, the wharf at Oakland Point, not drawn.
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (5 hand-read points). The centre of the mole's bundle of tracks, from the ferry slips to the shore at Seventh Street. The 1915 San Francisco sheet, corrected (sf1915-bay), puts the terminal within about 20 m of the 1949 sheet's.

segments.name: Seventh Street, Oakland
segments.method: Joined to sp-oakland-mole at its end; then along today's 7th Street centerline from -122.30845,37.80840 to Fallon Street (4126 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). In Seventh Street.

segments.name: Fallon Street to Melrose
segments.method: Joined to sp-seventh-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland East 1:24,000 (1949) (10 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the Southern Pacific's right of way as the 1949 sheet draws it, from the estuary shore past Fruitvale station toward Melrose. The sources name the ends (Fallon Street, Melrose Station) but not the track between, the link from Seventh Street at Fallon Street to the shore tracks is joined straight, and where Melrose Station stood isn't sourced, so this is dashed.

Part of it, from the junction with the San Francisco & Alameda west of San Leandro, may have opened in September 1869.

lines.name: Central Pacific trains, Oakland to Sacramento by the Benicia ferry
lines.summary: The low-level route to Sacramento: from the ferry at Oakland along the bay shore by Berkeley and Richmond to Port Costa, across the Carquinez Strait on the train ferry to Benicia, and on by Suisun and Davis.
lines.fate_note: Replaced on October 15, 1930 by the Martinez-Benicia bridge, a mile and a half east (Southern Pacific Bulletin, November-December 1930).
lines.notes: Drawn from the Oakland Mole; between the Mole's track at Sixteenth Street and today's line there is a short gap. The trains over the bridge after 1930 aren't drawn yet: no source read here shows them running to Sacramento. Its operator's change to the Southern Pacific (a lease of 1885) isn't dated from a source read here.

segments.name: Oakland Mole
segments.note: The Oakland Mole and its depot, opened in February 1881 (Wood, 1883, p. 631); before it, the Long Wharf, not drawn.
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (5 hand-read points). The centre of the mole's bundle of tracks, from the ferry slips to the shore at Seventh Street. The 1915 San Francisco sheet, corrected (sf1915-bay), puts the terminal within about 20 m of the 1949 sheet's.

segments.name: Oakland Mole to Sixteenth Street Station
segments.method: Joined to sp-oakland-mole at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points). The Southern Pacific main line from the mole through the West Oakland yard to Sixteenth Street Station, as the 1949 sheet draws it; the yard's many tracks make the line's exact track uncertain.
segments.notes: The Southern Pacific's main line, shared with its steam trains; its own dates aren't recorded here.

segments.name: West Oakland to Shell Mound
segments.method: GTFS shapes.txt: 6 shapes run by 191 trips, merged (kept where more than 25 m from track already drawn), simplified to 3 m; the stretch between Sixteenth Street, West Oakland and Shell Mound (data/present/extensions.json)
segments.notes: The Northern Railway's line north from West Oakland, opened in 1876; the Capitol Corridor's trains have run on it since 1991. Cut at today's track nearest the old Sixteenth Street station and at Shell Mound as the 1899 San Francisco sheet labels it (south of today's Emeryville station). The first biennial report's OCR reads "August 17, 1886", a misreading.

segments.name: Shell Mound to Emeryville
segments.method: GTFS shapes.txt: 6 shapes run by 191 trips, merged (kept where more than 25 m from track already drawn), simplified to 3 m; the stretch between Shell Mound and Port Costa (data/present/extensions.json)
segments.notes: The Northern Railway's line along the bay shore to Martinez, opened in 1878. Cut at Port Costa, where trains for Sacramento took the train ferry to Benicia from 1879 to 1930; the slip as the 1898 Karquines sheet places it, on today's track.

segments.name: Emeryville to Port Costa
segments.method: GTFS shapes.txt: 6 shapes run by 191 trips, merged (kept where more than 25 m from track already drawn), simplified to 3 m; the stretch between Shell Mound and Port Costa (data/present/extensions.json)
segments.notes: The Northern Railway's line along the bay shore to Martinez, opened in 1878. Cut at Port Costa, where trains for Sacramento took the train ferry to Benicia from 1879 to 1930; the slip as the 1898 Karquines sheet places it, on today's track.

segments.name: Port Costa to Benicia, the train ferry
segments.method: The shortest path over today's water from -122.18370,38.04600 to -122.16485,38.04465 (1822 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1 land and water), kept off the shore: the sources give the terminals, not the course. Port Costa's slip read off the 1898 Karquines sheet; Benicia's at the end of the waterfront track.
segments.notes: The ferries Solano (1879) and Contra Costa (1914) carried whole trains across the Carquinez Strait. The crossing is drawn as the shortest path over water between the slips, as the 1898 Karquines sheet places them.

segments.name: Benicia, the ferry slip to the line near Army Point
segments.method: OpenHistoricalMap way 200464960 (CC0, as of 2026-10-15), which OHM's mappers drew from USGS Napa CA 1902 topographic map, cut to -122.12801,38.04760; checked on USGS Karquines 1:62,500 (1898) and USGS Benicia 1:24,000 (1952). Cut where it meets today's track near Army Point. OpenHistoricalMap's way was traced from the 1902 Napa sheet (1:125,000); on the 1952 sheet it lies along the waterfront track.
segments.notes: From the slip along Benicia's waterfront to the main line, which today's track joins near Army Point. Trains to Sacramento left it for the bridge in 1930; when it last carried passengers isn't sourced.

lines.name: Claremont line

operators.name: Key System (the San Francisco, Oakland & San Jose Railway and its successors)

lines.summary: From the Key Route pier, and from 1939 the Bay Bridge, along Yerba Buena Avenue and Adeline Street, then 55th Street and Claremont Avenue to the Claremont Hotel on the Berkeley line.
lines.notes: Opened as the Claremont line in 1908 (the Oakland Tribune's retrospective of 1912); before that a branch ran from the ferry to Telegraph Avenue on 55th Street, from 1905 to 1907 (its first day isn't sourced). Night and Sunday service went to buses from November 7, 1954 (CPUC Decision No. 50731). The last trains ran in 1958 (HAER).

segments.name: Key Route Pier
segments.note: Over the Key Route pier to its ferries until January 15, 1939
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 3 m)); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The trestle runs straight from the shore, then curves to the ferry terminal.
segments.notes: Ferry trains ran to its end until the Bay Bridge opened to trains in January 1939; from then its land end carried the bridge trains. A 1933 fire is relayed via Wikipedia only.

segments.name: Transbay Terminal loop, San Francisco
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (23 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The loop as the 1950 sheet draws it ("KEY SYSTEM"): from the approach, north along the west side to the terminal's west end, through the six-track station facing Mission Street, around the east end and back south. Trains ran counter-clockwise, arriving at the station's east end.

segments.name: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge, lower deck
segments.method: Joined to bbr-sf-loop at its start; then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 2 m)); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (8 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From Rincon Hill across the bridge's lower deck, through the Yerba Buena Island tunnel, to where the tracks left the bridge on its south side at the Oakland end. The 1946-50 sheets draw the bridge, not the tracks on it; the tracks were on the south half of the lower deck.

segments.name: East Bay approach and yards
segments.method: Joined to bbr-bridge at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the south side of the bridge approach ("KEY SYSTEM" on the 1949 sheet) past the toll plaza to the East Bay yards, where the Key System's and the Interurban's tracks divided.

segments.name: East Bay yards to the old pier line
segments.method: Joined to bbr-east-approach at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then joined to key-pier at its start. From the East Bay yards over the bridge approach to the north side of the mole ("TRANSIT LINES" on the 1949 sheet), meeting the old pier line.

segments.name: Pier approach and subway to Poplar Junction
segments.method: Joined to key-pier at its start; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From the pier's land end under the Southern Pacific main line (the 1903 subway) to Poplar Junction, along the line the 1949 sheet draws there.

segments.name: Yerba Buena Avenue to San Pablo Avenue
segments.method: Joined to key-trunk-shore at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along Yerba Buena Avenue to the station at San Pablo Avenue.

segments.name: San Pablo Avenue to Adeline Street, by Linden Street
segments.method: Joined to key-yerba-buena at its end; then along today's Linden Street centerline from -122.27900,37.83100 to -122.27530,37.83550 (509 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 250 m where the street is cut today); then given point by point; checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). "Nearly north" from San Pablo Avenue, crossing Temescal Creek on Linden Street; drawn along today's Linden Street and joined straight to Adeline Street, which the sources don't place exactly.

segments.name: Adeline Street, to 55th Street
segments.method: Joined to key-linden-st at its end; then along today's Adeline Street centerline from -122.27450,37.83850 to 55th Street (61 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 250 m where the street is cut today); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Along Adeline Street to 55th Street, where the Claremont line left it.

segments.name: 55th, Vicente and 56th Streets, Adeline Street to Claremont Avenue
segments.method: Joined to key-adeline-55th at its end; then along today's 55th Street centerline from Adeline Street to Telegraph Avenue (1182 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (7 hand-read points); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). 55th Street is drawn along today's centerline to Telegraph Avenue; beyond it, where the freeway cut the streets since, by 55th Street, Vicente Street and 56th Street to Claremont Avenue as the 1949 sheet draws them.
segments.notes: The 55th Street branch ran from the ferry to Telegraph Avenue before the Claremont line was built (from 1905 to 1907: its first day isn't sourced). The block from Adeline Street to Market Street, where the 1954 buses began, is drawn on 55th Street too.

segments.name: Claremont Avenue, 56th Street to the Claremont Hotel
segments.method: Joined to key-55th-56th-st at its end; then along today's Claremont Avenue centerline from -122.25935,37.84101 to Domingo Avenue (2385 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland East 1:24,000 (1949). Along Claremont Avenue to the grounds of the Claremont Hotel at Domingo Avenue.
segments.notes: Up Claremont Avenue into Berkeley, to the grounds of the Claremont Hotel at Domingo Avenue.

lines.name: Encinal Avenue line
lines.summary: The Southern Pacific's electric Red Trains across Alameda along Central Avenue and Encinal Avenue, to the Alameda Mole and its ferries; from 1939 over the Fruitvale Bridge and the Bay Bridge to San Francisco.
lines.fate_note: Replaced by Key System buses from January 18, 1941.
lines.notes: The Interurban Electric Railway, a Southern Pacific company authorized in 1936 to take over these lines (CRC D28671), ran them until 1941; the day it took over isn't sourced here. Both Alameda lines were electrified in 1911 (CRC D33732, p. 8). Not yet drawn: the track west of Webster Street to the mole, and the east end to the Fruitvale Bridge (1939–41), which the sources don't place street by street. The June 1, 1911 opening is matched to this line because the trains ran "from High street to the Alameda mole", and the Encinal Avenue line ran to High Street (CRC D33732); no source of the day names Encinal Avenue.

segments.name: Alameda Mole
segments.note: Until the trains moved to the Bay Bridge
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (8 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (8 hand-read points); the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The railroad on the south jetty of the estuary's Deep Water Channel, from the ferry terminal to the junction at Alameda's west shore. Filled over by 1949, so traced from 1915.
segments.notes: The South Pacific Coast's mole, opened in 1884; the Southern Pacific's electric trains used it from 1911.

segments.name: Transbay Terminal loop, San Francisco
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (23 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The loop as the 1950 sheet draws it ("KEY SYSTEM"): from the approach, north along the west side to the terminal's west end, through the six-track station facing Mission Street, around the east end and back south. Trains ran counter-clockwise, arriving at the station's east end.

segments.name: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge, lower deck
segments.method: Joined to bbr-sf-loop at its start; then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 2 m)); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (8 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From Rincon Hill across the bridge's lower deck, through the Yerba Buena Island tunnel, to where the tracks left the bridge on its south side at the Oakland end. The 1946-50 sheets draw the bridge, not the tracks on it; the tracks were on the south half of the lower deck.

segments.name: East Bay approach and yards
segments.method: Joined to bbr-bridge at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the south side of the bridge approach ("KEY SYSTEM" on the 1949 sheet) past the toll plaza to the East Bay yards, where the Key System's and the Interurban's tracks divided.

segments.name: Interurban lead to 26th Street
segments.method: Joined to bbr-east-approach at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (7 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The Interurban's double-track lead from the bridge yards east to the Y at 26th Street, where it met the old Southern Pacific main line.

segments.name: Sixteenth Street Station to 26th Street
segments.method: Joined to sp-mole-16th-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points). Northeast from Sixteenth Street Station to the junction near the foot of 26th Street.

segments.name: Seventh Street, Oakland
segments.method: Joined to sp-oakland-mole at its end; then along today's 7th Street centerline from -122.30845,37.80840 to Fallon Street (4126 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). In Seventh Street.

segments.name: Fallon Street to Melrose
segments.note: To Fruitvale Junction, then the Fruitvale Bridge
segments.method: Joined to sp-seventh-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland East 1:24,000 (1949) (10 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the Southern Pacific's right of way as the 1949 sheet draws it, from the estuary shore past Fruitvale station toward Melrose. The sources name the ends (Fallon Street, Melrose Station) but not the track between, the link from Seventh Street at Fallon Street to the shore tracks is joined straight, and where Melrose Station stood isn't sourced, so this is dashed.

segments.name: Central Avenue and Encinal Avenue, Alameda
segments.method: Along today's Central Avenue centerline from Webster Street to Encinal Avenue (1150 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); then along today's Encinal Avenue centerline from Central Avenue to High Street (3102 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). In Central Avenue and Encinal Avenue.
segments.notes: The South Pacific Coast's main line of 1878 through Alameda; the Southern Pacific's electric trains ran on it from 1911.

lines.name: Lincoln Avenue line
lines.summary: The Southern Pacific's electric Red Trains across Alameda along Lincoln Avenue, to the Alameda Mole and its ferries; from 1939 over the Fruitvale Bridge and the Bay Bridge to San Francisco.
lines.fate_note: Replaced by Key System buses from January 18, 1941.
lines.notes: The Interurban Electric Railway, a Southern Pacific company authorized in 1936 to take over these lines (CRC D28671), ran them until 1941; the day it took over isn't sourced here. Both Alameda lines were electrified in 1911 (CRC D33732, p. 8). Not yet drawn: the track west of Webster Street to the mole, and the east end to the Fruitvale Bridge (1939–41), which the sources don't place street by street. The opening is the date announced the day before; no report of the day itself has been found, and earlier electric running on part of the line isn't ruled out.

segments.name: Alameda Mole
segments.note: Until the trains moved to the Bay Bridge
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (8 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (8 hand-read points); the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The railroad on the south jetty of the estuary's Deep Water Channel, from the ferry terminal to the junction at Alameda's west shore. Filled over by 1949, so traced from 1915.
segments.notes: The South Pacific Coast's mole, opened in 1884; the Southern Pacific's electric trains used it from 1911.

segments.name: Transbay Terminal loop, San Francisco
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (23 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The loop as the 1950 sheet draws it ("KEY SYSTEM"): from the approach, north along the west side to the terminal's west end, through the six-track station facing Mission Street, around the east end and back south. Trains ran counter-clockwise, arriving at the station's east end.

segments.name: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge, lower deck
segments.method: Joined to bbr-sf-loop at its start; then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 2 m)); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (8 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From Rincon Hill across the bridge's lower deck, through the Yerba Buena Island tunnel, to where the tracks left the bridge on its south side at the Oakland end. The 1946-50 sheets draw the bridge, not the tracks on it; the tracks were on the south half of the lower deck.

segments.name: East Bay approach and yards
segments.method: Joined to bbr-bridge at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the south side of the bridge approach ("KEY SYSTEM" on the 1949 sheet) past the toll plaza to the East Bay yards, where the Key System's and the Interurban's tracks divided.

segments.name: Interurban lead to 26th Street
segments.method: Joined to bbr-east-approach at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (7 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The Interurban's double-track lead from the bridge yards east to the Y at 26th Street, where it met the old Southern Pacific main line.

segments.name: Sixteenth Street Station to 26th Street
segments.method: Joined to sp-mole-16th-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points). Northeast from Sixteenth Street Station to the junction near the foot of 26th Street.

segments.name: Seventh Street, Oakland
segments.method: Joined to sp-oakland-mole at its end; then along today's 7th Street centerline from -122.30845,37.80840 to Fallon Street (4126 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). In Seventh Street.

segments.name: Fallon Street to Melrose
segments.note: To Fruitvale Junction, then the Fruitvale Bridge
segments.method: Joined to sp-seventh-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland East 1:24,000 (1949) (10 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the Southern Pacific's right of way as the 1949 sheet draws it, from the estuary shore past Fruitvale station toward Melrose. The sources name the ends (Fallon Street, Melrose Station) but not the track between, the link from Seventh Street at Fallon Street to the shore tracks is joined straight, and where Melrose Station stood isn't sourced, so this is dashed.

lines.name: Martinez–Benicia ferry
lines.summary: Auto and passenger ferries across the Carquinez Strait between Martinez and Benicia, every half hour in 1930; the last ferry in the Bay Area's state highway system.
lines.fate_note: Its last trip was on September 15, 1962, the day the Benicia-Martinez Bridge opened (California Highways and Public Works, 1962).
lines.notes: Run from 1913 by the Martinez-Benicia Ferry and Transportation Company, later by the American Toll Bridge Company and others, and from 1953 by the state (California Highways and Public Works, 1962). From early 1955 to late 1956 only a passenger ferry ran.

segments.name: Martinez to Benicia, across the Carquinez Strait
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS Benicia 1:24,000 (1952) (2 hand-read points). The two ends of the course the sheet draws, at the Benicia and Martinez piers.
segments.notes: Between the Municipal Wharf at Martinez and the foot of Fifth Street at Benicia, as the 1930 certificate names them; the course is the one the 1952 sheet draws, and the route had been "identical" since about 1922 (CRC Decision No. 22535).

lines.name: Mill Valley electric line
lines.summary: Third-rail electric trains from the ferry at Sausalito to Mill Valley, by the branch from Mill Valley Junction: the first of the North Shore's electric services.
lines.fate_note: Service ended on March 1, 1941, with the rest of the electric lines (CRC Decision No. 34457).
lines.notes: Run by the North Shore Railroad, then the Northwestern Pacific. Decision No. 34457 names only the Sausalito-San Rafael line; the Mill Valley branch is taken to have ended with it.

segments.notes: The North Pacific Coast's narrow-gauge main line from Sausalito, opened in 1875; the North Shore's electric trains ran over it from 1903, and both lines are drawn on it (decision 21). When it last carried passengers isn't sourced.

segments.name: Mill Valley branch, Mill Valley Junction to Mill Valley
segments.method: Joined to nwp-sausalito-almonte at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Tamalpais 1:62,500 (1941) (16 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol).
segments.notes: The North Pacific Coast's narrow-gauge line ran here before the electric line; when this track first carried passengers isn't sourced, so it shows with its lines' dates.

lines.name: Ninth Street line
lines.summary: The Southern Pacific's electric Red Trains from its Oakland ferry pier through Emeryville and along Ninth Street in West Berkeley to Albany and Thousand Oaks; over the Bay Bridge to San Francisco from 1939.
lines.fate_note: Replaced by Key System buses on July 26, 1941.
lines.notes: The Interurban Electric Railway, a Southern Pacific company authorized in 1936 to take over these lines (CRC D28671), ran them until 1941; the day it took over isn't sourced here. Opening: service over the loop by Solano Avenue to Ninth Street was planned to begin on Saturday, February 3, 1912, "if the trials justify" (San Francisco Call, February 2, 1912); no report of the day itself has been found. Wikipedia gives February 7, 1912, citing the Berkeley Gazette, not yet checked.

segments.name: Oakland Mole
segments.note: Until the trains moved to the Bay Bridge
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (5 hand-read points). The centre of the mole's bundle of tracks, from the ferry slips to the shore at Seventh Street. The 1915 San Francisco sheet, corrected (sf1915-bay), puts the terminal within about 20 m of the 1949 sheet's.

segments.name: Oakland Mole to Sixteenth Street Station
segments.note: Until the trains moved to the Bay Bridge
segments.method: Joined to sp-oakland-mole at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points). The Southern Pacific main line from the mole through the West Oakland yard to Sixteenth Street Station, as the 1949 sheet draws it; the yard's many tracks make the line's exact track uncertain.
segments.notes: The Southern Pacific's main line, shared with its steam trains; its own dates aren't recorded here.

segments.name: Sixteenth Street Station to 26th Street
segments.note: Until the trains moved to the Bay Bridge
segments.method: Joined to sp-mole-16th-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points). Northeast from Sixteenth Street Station to the junction near the foot of 26th Street.

segments.name: Transbay Terminal loop, San Francisco
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (23 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The loop as the 1950 sheet draws it ("KEY SYSTEM"): from the approach, north along the west side to the terminal's west end, through the six-track station facing Mission Street, around the east end and back south. Trains ran counter-clockwise, arriving at the station's east end.

segments.name: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge, lower deck
segments.method: Joined to bbr-sf-loop at its start; then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 2 m)); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (8 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From Rincon Hill across the bridge's lower deck, through the Yerba Buena Island tunnel, to where the tracks left the bridge on its south side at the Oakland end. The 1946-50 sheets draw the bridge, not the tracks on it; the tracks were on the south half of the lower deck.

segments.name: East Bay approach and yards
segments.method: Joined to bbr-bridge at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the south side of the bridge approach ("KEY SYSTEM" on the 1949 sheet) past the toll plaza to the East Bay yards, where the Key System's and the Interurban's tracks divided.

segments.name: Interurban lead to 26th Street
segments.method: Joined to bbr-east-approach at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (7 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The Interurban's double-track lead from the bridge yards east to the Y at 26th Street, where it met the old Southern Pacific main line.

segments.name: 26th Street to 34th Street
segments.method: Joined to sp-16th-st-26th-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points). North by Wood Street to 34th Street.

segments.name: Wood Street, 34th Street to Ninth Street junction
segments.method: Joined to sp-26th-st-34th-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (7 hand-read points). North along the tracks by Wood Street from 34th Street, curving northeast to the junction at Stanford Avenue and Hollis Street (Ninth Street junction), where the 1949 sheet shows the track splitting north (Ninth Street line) and northeast (Stanford Avenue).

segments.name: Ninth Street junction to Heinz Avenue, Emeryville
segments.method: Joined to sp-wood-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (8 hand-read points). North from Ninth Street junction through Emeryville to Heinz Avenue, read by hand where the 1949 sheet draws the track among others.

segments.name: Ninth Street, Heinz Avenue to Harrison Street
segments.method: Along today's Ninth Street centerline from Heinz Avenue to Harrison Street (3198 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Richmond 1:24,000 (1949). In Ninth Street.

segments.name: Albany, Solano Avenue to Harrison Street
segments.method: Joined to sp-ninth-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (8 hand-read points); then joined to sp-solano-ave-west at its end; the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The 1915 sheet draws a railroad here, west of San Pablo Avenue, but places it only roughly; its north end stops short of Solano Avenue on the sheet, and the last stretch to Solano Avenue is joined straight.
segments.notes: Part of the loop to Thousand Oaks, planned to open February 3, 1912 (San Francisco Call, February 2, 1912); its opening isn't confirmed, so it borrows its lines' dates.

segments.name: Solano Avenue, Thousand Oaks Station to San Pablo Avenue
segments.method: Along today's Solano Avenue centerline from Colusa Avenue to San Pablo Avenue (1710 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Richmond 1:24,000 (1949). In Solano Avenue, across San Pablo Avenue.
segments.notes: Part of the loop to Thousand Oaks, planned to open February 3, 1912 (San Francisco Call, February 2, 1912); its opening isn't confirmed, so it borrows its lines' dates.

lines.name: No. 40 San Mateo
lines.system_name: Market Street Railway and United Railroads
lines.summary: The San Mateo interurban: from 5th and Market out Mission St through Daly City and Colma, then on its own right of way by the cemeteries, San Bruno and Millbrae to Burlingame, and through the streets of San Mateo to Main St.
lines.fate_note: Abandoned on January 16, 1949, the last day of operation being January 15, 1949 (the San Francisco PUC's report for 1948-49).
lines.notes: Its opening to San Mateo isn't sourced; the map draws it from October 31, 1903, when the Street Railway Journal describes the cars running (decision 20). In 1903 it reached the city by the San Francisco & San Mateo's streets of 1892, which aren't drawn yet, so until 1909 it is drawn from Daly City. Its streets in San Mateo are O'Shaughnessy's of 1929; the ones before aren't sourced.

running.note: "The cars at the present time are operated every half-hour" to San Mateo.
"5th and Market via 5th to Mission to Colma to Cemeteries to San Mateo."

Map of the city of San Mateo, showing the latest additions and subdivisions (1912); San Mateo County subdivision maps; USGS San Mateo 1939 topographic map, https://ngmdb.usgs.gov; checked on USGS San Francisco South 1:24,000 (1950), USGS Montara Mountain 1:24,000 (1949) and USGS San Mateo 1:24,000 (1949). lines.name: No. 6 Haight Street and Masonic Avenue
lines.system_name: Market Street Railway and United Railroads
lines.summary: In 1909 the "Masonic" line ran out Hayes St, Fillmore St and Oak St (back on Page St), then by Masonic Ave, Frederick St, Clayton St, Carl St and Stanyan St "to Parnassas Ave. to Affiliated Colleges"; Manley calls the name "a misnomer, as it runs for but three blocks on Masonic Ave". By 1929 it ran out Haight St and on to 9th Ave and Pacheco St.
lines.fate_note: Motor coaches from July 4, 1948; trolley coaches from 1949.

lines.name: No. 9 Alameda via Park Street
lines.system_name: East Bay streetcars (Oakland Traction and its successors)
lines.summary: From downtown Oakland out East 14th St and 23rd Ave across the Park Street bridge to Alameda (the East Alameda line in 1933). It stopped when the county closed the bridge to cars over ten tons on May 2, 1933 (Decision 26059). In 1931 its downtown loop by 5th Ave and 8th St was given up for 1st Ave, 12th St and 13th St (the old loop isn't drawn: 5th Ave no longer reaches 8th St). The approach to the old Park Street bridge, rebuilt in 1935, isn't drawn.

lines.name: North Pacific Coast, Sausalito to the Russian River
lines.summary: A narrow-gauge railroad from the ferry at Sausalito over White's Hill to Point Reyes, around Tomales Bay to Tomales, and through the redwoods to the Russian River at Duncans Mills (1877), later Cazadero (1886).
lines.fate_note: Trains between Point Reyes and Monte Rio ended on April 3, 1930 (CRC Decision No. 22672), and between Manor and Point Reyes on August 1, 1933, replaced by Pacific Greyhound's stages (Decision No. 34457).
lines.notes: Drawn as its own line over the track it shared with the North Shore's electric trains from 1903 (decision 21). How far the trains to Point Reyes ran over the electrified track in later years isn't sourced; the map draws the line from Sausalito, as the North Pacific Coast built it, until its last trains in 1933. Not drawn: Sheridan to Duncans Mills and Cazadero, which no sheet of the line's years shows (a map to georeference by hand), and the tunnels at White's Hill and into Sonoma County. When the North Shore and then the Northwestern Pacific took it over isn't sourced here.

segments.notes: The North Pacific Coast's narrow-gauge main line from Sausalito, opened in 1875; the North Shore's electric trains ran over it from 1903, and both lines are drawn on it (decision 21). When it last carried passengers isn't sourced.

segments.name: San Anselmo to Manor, by Fairfax
segments.method: Joined to nwp-corte-madera-san-anselmo at its end; then OpenHistoricalMap way 200221492 (CC0, as of 2026-10-15), which OHM's mappers drew from USGS Tamalpais 1897 topographic map, cut from -122.56210,37.97739 and to -122.59200,37.99200; checked on USGS Tamalpais 1:62,500 (1897) and USGS Tamalpais 1:62,500 (1941). Cut at San Anselmo and at Manor as the 1941 sheet labels them. OpenHistoricalMap's way here was traced from the 1897 15-minute sheet: on the 1941 sheet it runs 40-60 m north-east of the track, and a straight join of 97 m meets the electric line's track at San Anselmo. It needs a fit (decision 12) or a trace from a better map.
segments.notes: On the North Pacific Coast's main line from Sausalito. The electric line ran on to Manor in later years (not drawn), so when this track last carried passengers isn't sourced.

segments.name: Manor to Point Reyes, by White's Hill, San Geronimo, Lagunitas and Camp Taylor
segments.method: OpenHistoricalMap ways 200221492, 202387716, 202387717, 202387713 (CC0, as of 2026-10-15), which OHM's mappers drew from USGS Tamalpais 1897 topographic map, cut from -122.59200,37.99200 and to -122.80600,38.06800; checked on USGS Tamalpais 1:62,500 (1897), USGS Petaluma 1:62,500 (1914) and USGS Point Reyes 1:48,000 (1916). Cut at Manor (1941 sheet) and at Point Reyes Station (1916 sheet). From Manor to White's Hill (about 2 km) OpenHistoricalMap's way was traced from the 1897 15-minute sheet and is likely tens of metres off, as it is from San Anselmo to Manor; beyond, its ways follow the railroad on the 1914 and 1916 sheets.
segments.notes: Over White's Hill by a tunnel (Marin County history, pp. 147-148); the tunnel isn't marked separately here.

segments.name: Tomales to Occidental (Howard's), by Valley Ford and Freestone

segments.name: Monte Rio to Sheridan, along the Russian River

segments.method: OpenHistoricalMap way 202387715 (CC0, as of 2026-10-15), cut from -123.01000,38.46420; checked on USGS Duncans Mills 1:31,680 (1945). Cut at Monte Rio as the 1945 sheet labels it.

lines.name: Northwestern Pacific trains to Eureka, from San Rafael
lines.summary: The Northwestern Pacific's trains north from San Rafael by Petaluma, Santa Rosa and Healdsburg to Cloverdale, and on to Willits and Eureka.
lines.fate_note: The Public Utilities Commission let the railroad discontinue Trains Nos. 3 and 4 between San Rafael and Willits on October 21, 1958, effective twenty days later; the last train isn't dated in the order, so the line closes on or about November 1958 (decision 17).
lines.notes: When these trains began isn't sourced; the map draws them from 1935, the first date a source shows them (decision 20). In 1941 they started at Sausalito and ran by San Rafael (not drawn here); by 1958 they started at San Rafael, with a bus from San Francisco. North of Cloverdale the line runs on beyond the Bay Area.

running.note: "there will still remain in service two trains in each direction between San Francisco and Eureka, as well as trains on the Guerneville Branch."
Its trains "between Sausalito and Eureka by way of San Rafael".
"Train No. 4 operates northbound from San Rafael to Eureka three days a week".

lines.name: Peninsula trains, San Francisco to San José
lines.summary: Trains between San Francisco and San José: the San Francisco & San Jose Railroad's from 1863, the Southern Pacific's from 1870. They left the city through the Mission, the Bernal Cut and Ocean View until the Bayshore Cutoff opened in 1907, and reached San José's Cahill Street station from the end of 1935. Caltrain runs on the same track.
lines.fate_note: On July 1, 1980 Caltrans took over the Peninsula Commute Service, with the Southern Pacific still running the trains; it became today's Caltrain (Caltrain milestones).
lines.notes: The San Francisco end moved: at 18th and Valencia Sts at first (Caltrain), the Mission (the directories), Fourth and Brannan Sts from February 14, 1864, Market and Valencia Sts by 1867, and Fourth and Townsend Sts by 1876 (Langley's directory). Only the way out of the city that the 1899 sheet draws is mapped; the earlier approaches aren't. The first train, on October 17, 1863, ran only to Big Tree Station on San Francisquito Creek; Caltrain gives regular service to Mayfield that October. In San José the trains ended at the Market Street station until 1935.

lines.name: Petaluma & Santa Rosa, Sebastopol to Santa Rosa
lines.summary: Electric cars from Sebastopol by Gravenstein and Llano, then beside Sebastopol Ave into Santa Rosa, up Olive St and along Fourth St to McDonald Ave.
lines.fate_note: Its passenger and express service ended under the Railroad Commission's order of May 31, 1932 (Decision No. 24818), as of July 1, 1932 (Decision No. 24983); its freight trains ran on.
lines.notes: Opens on JOE's November 19, 1904, which names no terminals; Borden and Ellison and Sievers say the first cars ran to the California Northwestern's crossing at the Santa Rosa city limits (November 29 or December 1). Between Leddy and the crossing it is drawn on Sebastopol Rd's centerline, the road it ran beside. By 1927, 18 round trips a day (Borden, p. 25).

segments.name: Into Sebastopol, along the Gravenstein Highway and Main St
segments.note: Through cars from Petaluma ran into Santa Rosa at first (Borden; Ellison and Sievers).
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS Sebastopol 1:24,000 (1954) (7 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Sebastopol 1:24,000 (1954) (18 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Sebastopol 1:24,000 (1954) (5 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Sebastopol 1:24,000 (1954) (2 hand-read points). Beside the Gravenstein Highway, then in Main St to the depot, as the 1954 sheet draws it.
segments.notes: In the streets of Sebastopol, as a 1941 photo caption in Borden has it. Its passenger cars ended on July 1, 1932; the track went on carrying freight, and when it was taken up isn't sourced here.

segments.name: Sebastopol to Leddy, by Gravenstein and Llano
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS Sebastopol 1:24,000 (1954) (5 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Sebastopol 1:24,000 (1954) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Sebastopol 1:24,000 (1954) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Sebastopol 1:24,000 (1954) (20 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The track the 1954 sheet labels Petaluma & Santa Rosa, by Gravenstein and Llano to Leddy, which the 1935 sheet shows beside the Northwestern Pacific's own Sebastopol branch.
segments.notes: Its passenger cars ended on July 1, 1932; the track went on carrying freight, and when it was taken up isn't sourced here.

segments.name: Leddy to the Northwestern Pacific's crossing, along Sebastopol Rd
segments.method: Along today's Sebastopol Road and Sebastopol Avenue centerline from -122.77201,38.42455 to -122.72128,38.43160 (4522 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Sebastopol 1:48,000 (1935) and USGS Santa Rosa 1:62,500 (1916). Borden: "street and side of the road running" on Sebastopol Ave between Santa Rosa and Leddy; the 1916 and 1935 sheets draw the line beside the road, here drawn on its centerline to the Northwestern Pacific's crossing.
segments.notes: The cars ran only to this crossing, then the California Northwestern's, at the Santa Rosa city limits, until the night of March 1, 1905 (Borden; Ellison and Sievers). Borden: the track was abandoned between Olive St and Stop 45 on May 20, 1946, when Sebastopol Ave was widened, and the line then used the Northwestern Pacific's Sebastopol branch into Santa Rosa.

segments.name: Sebastopol Ave and Olive St, Santa Rosa
segments.note: Until the night of March 1, 1905 the cars stopped at the California Northwestern's crossing, which the steam road wouldn't let them cross (Borden; Street Railway Journal).
segments.method: Along today's Sebastopol Avenue centerline from -122.72128,38.43160 to Olive Street (201 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); then along today's Olive Street and Wilson Street centerline from Sebastopol Avenue to 4th Street (623 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 250 m where the street is cut today); checked on USGS Santa Rosa 1:24,000 (1954). Sebastopol Ave to Olive St and Olive St to Fourth St (Borden); Olive St ran on to Fourth St at Wilson St on the 1954 sheet, where today's freeway cuts it.
segments.notes: Opened when the first car crossed the California Northwestern's track "shortly after midnight" after the fight of March 1, 1905 (Borden). The depot was at Olive St (Borden, p. 26).

segments.name: Fourth St, Santa Rosa, to McDonald Ave
segments.note: Fourth St's cars ended on December 31, 1931 (Borden), under the order of December 14, 1931 (Decision No. 24310).
segments.method: Along today's 4th Street centerline from Wilson Street to McDonald Avenue (1699 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 300 m where the street is cut today); checked on USGS Santa Rosa 1:24,000 (1954). In Fourth St to the terminus at McDonald Ave (Borden; CRC Decision No. 24310), across today's freeway, where Overture has no 4th St.
segments.notes: The Railroad Commission's order of December 14, 1931 let the company abandon Fourth St from Wilson St to McDonald Ave; Borden has its cars end on December 31, 1931.

lines.notes: Not yet drawn: the 1924 extension beyond Piedmont Avenue to Oakland Avenue in Piedmont, whose streets come only from secondary sources. The last trains ran in 1958 (HAER); April 19 or 20, 1958 is given only by later sources.

segments.name: Key Route Pier
segments.note: Ferry trains, until the Bay Bridge opened to trains
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 3 m)); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The trestle runs straight from the shore, then curves to the ferry terminal.
segments.notes: Ferry trains ran to its end until the Bay Bridge opened to trains in January 1939; from then its land end carried the bridge trains. A 1933 fire is relayed via Wikipedia only.

segments.name: Transbay Terminal loop, San Francisco
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (23 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The loop as the 1950 sheet draws it ("KEY SYSTEM"): from the approach, north along the west side to the terminal's west end, through the six-track station facing Mission Street, around the east end and back south. Trains ran counter-clockwise, arriving at the station's east end.

segments.name: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge, lower deck
segments.method: Joined to bbr-sf-loop at its start; then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 2 m)); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (8 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From Rincon Hill across the bridge's lower deck, through the Yerba Buena Island tunnel, to where the tracks left the bridge on its south side at the Oakland end. The 1946-50 sheets draw the bridge, not the tracks on it; the tracks were on the south half of the lower deck.

segments.name: East Bay approach and yards
segments.method: Joined to bbr-bridge at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the south side of the bridge approach ("KEY SYSTEM" on the 1949 sheet) past the toll plaza to the East Bay yards, where the Key System's and the Interurban's tracks divided.

segments.name: East Bay yards to the old pier line
segments.method: Joined to bbr-east-approach at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then joined to key-pier at its start. From the East Bay yards over the bridge approach to the north side of the mole ("TRANSIT LINES" on the 1949 sheet), meeting the old pier line.

segments.name: Pier approach and subway to Poplar Junction
segments.method: Joined to key-pier at its start; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From the pier's land end under the Southern Pacific main line (the 1903 subway) to Poplar Junction, along the line the 1949 sheet draws there.

segments.name: Yerba Buena Avenue to San Pablo Avenue

lines.name: Sacramento Northern trains, San Francisco to Bay Point and Sacramento
lines.summary: Electric trains from the Key Route pier, and from 1939 the Bay Bridge, by 40th St and Shafter Ave in Oakland, through the hills by Shepherd Canyon and the Redwood Peak tunnel, to Moraga, Walnut Creek, Concord and Bay Point, and from September 1913 on by West Pittsburg, the train ferry from Mallard to Chipps Island, Montezuma and Rio Vista Junction to Sacramento, until 1940. Drawn to the Yolo County line, where it leaves the Bay Area (decision 16).
lines.fate_note: Replaced by Pacific Greyhound buses in 1941 (CRC Decision No. 34232). Freight trains used the line through the Oakland hills until 1957.
lines.notes: The last day, June 30, 1941, rests on a railfan magazine's reminiscence of 1945; the Railroad Commission authorized the end in May 1941. Through service to Sacramento, by the Chipps Island ferry, ran from September 3, 1913 (the first through train on July 2) to on or about August 1940 (Decision No. 33416); after that the trains ran to Pittsburg. The Pittsburg branch itself isn't drawn yet: its opening isn't sourced.

segments.name: Key Route Pier
segments.note: Over the Key Route's pier to its ferries until January 15, 1939
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 3 m)); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The trestle runs straight from the shore, then curves to the ferry terminal.
segments.notes: Ferry trains ran to its end until the Bay Bridge opened to trains in January 1939; from then its land end carried the bridge trains. A 1933 fire is relayed via Wikipedia only.

segments.name: Transbay Terminal loop, San Francisco
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (23 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The loop as the 1950 sheet draws it ("KEY SYSTEM"): from the approach, north along the west side to the terminal's west end, through the six-track station facing Mission Street, around the east end and back south. Trains ran counter-clockwise, arriving at the station's east end.

segments.name: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge, lower deck
segments.method: Joined to bbr-sf-loop at its start; then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 2 m)); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (8 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From Rincon Hill across the bridge's lower deck, through the Yerba Buena Island tunnel, to where the tracks left the bridge on its south side at the Oakland end. The 1946-50 sheets draw the bridge, not the tracks on it; the tracks were on the south half of the lower deck.

segments.name: East Bay approach and yards
segments.method: Joined to bbr-bridge at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the south side of the bridge approach ("KEY SYSTEM" on the 1949 sheet) past the toll plaza to the East Bay yards, where the Key System's and the Interurban's tracks divided.

segments.name: East Bay yards to the old pier line
segments.method: Joined to bbr-east-approach at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then joined to key-pier at its start. From the East Bay yards over the bridge approach to the north side of the mole ("TRANSIT LINES" on the 1949 sheet), meeting the old pier line.

segments.name: Pier approach and subway to Poplar Junction
segments.method: Joined to key-pier at its start; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From the pier's land end under the Southern Pacific main line (the 1903 subway) to Poplar Junction, along the line the 1949 sheet draws there.

segments.name: Yerba Buena Avenue to San Pablo Avenue
segments.method: Joined to key-trunk-shore at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along Yerba Buena Avenue to the station at San Pablo Avenue.

segments.name: Yerba Buena Avenue and 40th Street to Shafter Avenue
segments.note: Over the Key Route's tracks on 40th St
segments.method: Joined to key-yerba-buena at its end; then along today's Yerba Buena Avenue centerline from -122.27980,37.82960 to 40th Street (260 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); then along today's 40th Street centerline from Yerba Buena Avenue to -122.25978,37.82846 (1450 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 250 m where the street is cut today); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). segments.name: Rockridge to Lake Temescal and Montclair

segments.name: Shepherd Canyon and the Redwood Peak tunnel
segments.method: Joined to sn-rockridge-temescal at its end; then along today's Shepherd Canyon Road centerline from -122.20530,37.82450 to -122.18479,37.83578 (2831 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); then given point by point; checked on USGS Oakland East 1:24,000 (1949).
segments.notes: Up Shepherd Canyon, whose road today follows the old right-of-way, then through the 3,458 ft tunnel under Redwood Peak to Eastport. The canyon is drawn along today's Shepherd Canyon Road and checked on the 1949 sheet; the tunnel is drawn straight between its portals and is approximate.

segments.name: Eastport to Moraga and Lafayette
segments.method: Joined to sn-shepherd-canyon at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Concord 1:62,500 (1942) (17 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Concord 1:62,500 (1942) (13 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Concord 1:62,500 (1942) (21 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol).
segments.notes: Down the San Leandro Creek valley to Valle Vista and Moraga, then by St Mary's College and Burton to Lafayette, traced from the 1942 Concord sheet, which falls within about 50 m of today's streets here. Opened east of Lafayette in 1911, as the Oakland & Antioch's local line (Bay Point to Concord from February 1911, to Walnut Creek by about September, to Lafayette by December 19); those dates aren't confirmed enough to draw yet, so the track shows from the through service of 1913.

segments.name: Saranap to Walnut Creek and Concord
segments.method: Joined to sn-eastport-lafayette at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Walnut Creek 1:24,000 (1949) (23 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Walnut Creek 1:24,000 (1949) (19 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Walnut Creek 1:24,000 (1949) (12 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol).
segments.notes: Through Saranap, Walnut Creek and Las Juntas to Bancroft, then by Meinert into Concord, traced from the 1949 Walnut Creek sheet. Opened east of Lafayette in 1911, as the Oakland & Antioch's local line (Bay Point to Concord from February 1911, to Walnut Creek by about September, to Lafayette by December 19); those dates aren't confirmed enough to draw yet, so the track shows from the through service of 1913.

segments.name: Concord to Bay Point (Port Chicago)
segments.method: Joined to sn-saranap-concord at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Port Chicago 1:24,000 (1951) (23 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol).
segments.notes: North by Clyde to Bay Point, renamed Port Chicago in 1931, traced from the 1951 Port Chicago sheet. Opened east of Lafayette in 1911, as the Oakland & Antioch's local line (Bay Point to Concord from February 1911, to Walnut Creek by about September, to Lafayette by December 19); those dates aren't confirmed enough to draw yet, so the track shows from the through service of 1913.

segments.name: Bay Point to West Pittsburg
segments.method: Joined to sn-concord-bay-point at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Port Chicago 1:24,000 (1951) (11 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Honker Bay 1:24,000 (1953) (15 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Honker Bay 1:24,000 (1953) (7 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Honker Bay 1:24,000 (1953) (3 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Honker Bay 1:24,000 (1953) (9 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Honker Bay 1:24,000 (1953) (3 hand-read points). The southernmost of three parallel lines (the Southern Pacific, the Santa Fe and this), labelled Sacramento Northern on the sheet, where the track still carried freight.
segments.notes: East from Bay Point (Port Chicago from 1931) beside the Southern Pacific and the Santa Fe to West Pittsburg, where the line to Mallard and the ferry left the Pittsburg branch. Traced from the 1953 Honker Bay and 1951 Port Chicago sheets.

segments.name: West Pittsburg to Mallard
segments.note: Trains north of West Pittsburg ended on or about August 1940: the Railroad Commission's Decision No. 33416 of August 20, 1940 let them stop on five days' notice, effective five days from its date; the last day isn't sourced (decision 17)
segments.method: Joined to sn-bay-point-west-pittsburg at its end; then OpenHistoricalMap ways 199932059, 199932054, 199932053, 199932051, 199932057, 199932050, 199932049, 199932048 (CC0, as of 2026-10-15); checked on USGS Honker Bay 1:24,000 (1953).
segments.notes: North from the Pittsburg branch at West Pittsburg to the ferry slip at Mallard, on Suisun Bay.

segments.name: Train ferry, Mallard to Chipps Island
segments.note: By the train ferry across Suisun Bay. Trains north of West Pittsburg ended on or about August 1940: the Railroad Commission's Decision No. 33416 of August 20, 1940 let them stop on five days' notice, effective five days from its date; the last day isn't sourced (decision 17)
segments.method: Traced by eye from USGS Honker Bay 1:24,000 (1953) (2 hand-read points). The train ferry's course as the 1953 sheet draws it (FERRY), straight between the slips at Mallard and on Chipps Island.
segments.notes: The ferry carried the trains across Suisun Bay between the slips at Mallard and on Chipps Island.

segments.name: Chipps Island to the Yolo County line
segments.note: Trains north of West Pittsburg ended on or about August 1940: the Railroad Commission's Decision No. 33416 of August 20, 1940 let them stop on five days' notice, effective five days from its date; the last day isn't sourced (decision 17)
segments.notes: From the ferry slip on Chipps Island north across the Montezuma Hills by Montezuma and Rio Vista Junction, then northeast past Dozier toward the Yolo Bypass and Sacramento. Drawn to the Yolo County line, where it leaves the Bay Area (decision 16).
